data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 369090fbce5900618b0bb78d8b261699f7b02c1e

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

The skip-review-check (COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md Step 0.5) should set SKIP_REVIEW=true only when ALL files in the commit are allowlisted for skip. New (untracked) files staged for the first commit count as "non-allowlisted code changes" and must force SKIP_REVIEW=false.

#### Actual Behavior

The check pipes `git diff HEAD --name-only` into `dso skip-review-check`. `git diff HEAD --name-only` does not list untracked files, so when the only non-allowlisted change is an untracked new file (e.g., a new test file alongside allowlisted tracked changes), SKIP_REVIEW is incorrectly set to true. User confirmed during a strict-doc commit run: "SKIP_REVIEW=true was a false positive because git diff HEAD --name-only didn't see the untracked test file."

In the observed incident the downstream review still ran (Step 5 was reached anyway), but the skip-check itself returned the wrong answer and would skip review on a different code path that actually honors it.

### 3. Action History and Workarounds

* **Known Workarounds:** None — the bug is silent; correct behavior depended on a downstream step running unconditionally.

### 7. Additional Details

Suggested fix: union `git diff --cached --name-only` with `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (and HEAD-vs-working-tree) so the file set passed to skip-review-check includes untracked-but-staged-or-pending files.
data.title: skip-review-check: detect non-allowlisted changes -> false positive when only new file is untracked (git diff HEAD --name-only misses untracked)
